summary: Both spectra show the 2H-WS2 set: 2LA(M) ~350–351, E2g ~355, A1g ~417–420, LA(M) ~176, plus the Si substrate line at 520.8–520.9 cm-1. The two spots differ mainly in three things. (1) The A1g–E2g separation is 62.0 cm-1 on spot 1 and 64.7 cm-1 on spot 2. E2g is unchanged (355.3 vs 355.4); the shift is in A1g (417.3 vs 420.1). (2) On spot 1 the 2LA(M) band dominates the E2g band; on spot 2 it is a minor shoulder. (3) The Si line is about 10x stronger on spot 1 (fitted area 6762 vs 664), so spot 1 is much less absorbing. Spot 1 is consistent with a monolayer and is the most likely assignment, but this spectrum alone cannot exclude a bilayer. Spot 2 is clearly multilayer and thick. Confirming the layer number needs PL, ultra-low-frequency Raman or AFM, none of which is in this folder.

observations.finding: Spot 1 peak assignments from three-Lorentzian fits over 330–440 cm-1: 2LA(M) at 351.09 cm-1 (FWHM 8.9, area ~25,200); E2g^1 at 355.28 cm-1 (FWHM 4.0, area ~2,600, a shoulder on the high-frequency side of the 2LA band); A1g at 417.28 cm-1 (FWHM 4.6, area ~5,800). The E2g–A1g separation is 62.00 cm-1.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian least-squares fits, spectrum_spot1.csv, 330–440 cm-1 window. Centre errors ±0.02–0.07 cm-1 (stderr). Changing the window (325–450, 330–440, 335–430) or adding a pedestal changes the separation by less than 0.02 cm-1. Pseudo-Voigt lineshapes give the same centres (2LA 351.09, E2g 355.29, A1g 417.28), with eta≈0.99, i.e. the bands are Lorentzian.

observations.finding: Spot 2 (thick region) assignments: 2LA(M) at 349.85 cm-1 (FWHM 8.7, area ~7,200); E2g^1 at 355.38 cm-1 (FWHM 4.1, area ~4,400); A1g at 420.08 cm-1 (FWHM 4.4, area ~7,800). Separation 64.70 cm-1, stable to the same window and pedestal changes (±0.02 cm-1).
observations.evidence: Same fitting procedure as spot 1, spectrum_spot2.csv. Pseudo-Voigt check gives identical centres and a separation of 64.70 cm-1.

observations.finding: The thickness-sensitive difference is in A1g, not E2g. E2g is 355.28 (spot 1) vs 355.38 (spot 2), a 0.1 cm-1 difference, while A1g is 417.28 vs 420.08, a 2.8 cm-1 downshift on spot 1. The separation difference (2.7 cm-1) comes almost entirely from A1g.
observations.evidence: Centre differences from the fits above. Calibration offsets cancel in the difference, so the separation is calibration-independent.

observations.finding: The 2LA(M) to E2g intensity ratio is about 9.6 on spot 1 (25,213 / 2,615) and about 1.7 on spot 2 (7,257 / 4,345). Since 514.5 nm (2.41 eV) lies close to the WS2 B-exciton resonance, the 2LA(M) band is resonantly enhanced, and that enhancement is expected to be stronger for thin flakes. A dominant 351 band on spot 1 is therefore consistent with a monolayer under resonance, but this intensity ratio is not a calibrated thickness metric.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fit areas. Resonance enhancement and laser power/heating are not controlled in this dataset.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), discussion of 514.5 nm WS2 spectra (recalled from memory; not re-checked in this session)

observations.finding: Si substrate line at 520.8–520.9 cm-1 (FWHM ~3.5). Fitted area 6,762 on spot 1 vs 664 on spot 2 (peak height 1,236 vs 117). The Si signal is about 10x stronger on spot 1, i.e. the thin region absorbs much less of the 514.5 nm excitation and Si Raman signal than the thick region does.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fit over 500–540 cm-1, both spectra. Peak position is 0.1–0.2 cm-1 above the standard 520.7 cm-1 Si reference, which gives the calibration offset. Without a bare SiO2/Si reference spectrum the absolute attenuation cannot be quantified.

observations.finding: LA(M) band near 176 cm-1 is present on both spots (spot 1: 176.04, area ~1,900; spot 2: 175.64, area ~970). The LA(M)/E2g area ratio is about 0.72 on spot 1 vs 0.22 on spot 2, so the LA(M) band is relatively stronger on the thin region, as expected for resonance-enhanced LA(M) in thin WS2. The 2LA(M) band at ~351 is roughly twice the LA(M) frequency (2 × 176 ≈ 352), which is a rough consistency check on the overtone assignment.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fit over 150–200 cm-1. Spot 2 LA(M) is weak (height ~52 counts) and its fit is less constrained (redchi 142).

observations.finding: Spot 1 shows a sloped continuum that spot 2 lacks. Median counts are 402 (120–300 cm-1), 480 (440–510 cm-1) and 498 (530–600 cm-1) on spot 1, against 405, 403 and 390 on spot 2. The excess is about 80 counts from 440 cm-1 upwards.
observations.evidence: Median in fixed windows. 530–600 slope is −0.03 counts/cm-1 on spot 1 and −0.16 on spot 2, so the spot 1 continuum is elevated but not tilted in that window. The 120–600 cm-1 window only covers emission near the laser line (~514–530 nm), so a PL band at ~2 eV (~620 nm, ~3300 cm-1 shift) cannot be seen here. The origin of the continuum is undetermined.

observations.finding: Assignments: 176 cm-1 LA(M) (M-point longitudinal acoustic); ~351 2LA(M) (two-phonon overtone, resonantly enhanced at 514.5 nm); ~355 E2g^1 (in-plane); ~417–420 A1g (out-of-plane); ~520.8 Si substrate first-order. The four WS2 modes are the expected 2H-WS2 set. Spot 1 reads as thin and spot 2 as thick.
observations.evidence: Peak positions and widths listed above; Si line position matches the standard 520.7 cm-1 reference within 0.2 cm-1.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), layer-dependent WS2 Raman table/figure (recalled from memory; verify); Si reference 520.7 cm-1: Temple & Hathaway, Phys. Rev. B 7, 3685 (1973) (recalled from memory; verify)

observations.finding: Monolayer vs thick. The E2g–A1g separation for monolayer WS2 is reported at about 60–62 cm-1, rising toward ~64–65 cm-1 for thicker, bulk-like flakes. Spot 1 (62.0) sits at the upper edge of the monolayer range and is clearly below spot 2 (64.7), so spot 1 is thinner than spot 2 and is compatible with monolayer, but the separation alone cannot separate 1L from 2L. The thickness-dependent stiffening of A1g is attributed to interlayer coupling (the MoS2 analogue is Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010)).
observations.evidence: Δ = 62.0 (spot 1) vs 64.7 (spot 2), robust to fit choices to ±0.02 cm-1. Systematic uncertainty from line overlap is probably ~±0.5 cm-1, since the E2g shoulder is only 4 cm-1 from 2LA. The absolute literature ranges are from memory and need checking against the cited papers.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013) (recalled from memory; verify ranges); Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010) for the A1g layer-dependence trend in MoS2 (recalled from memory; verify)

properties.name: layers
properties.value: spot 1: 1 (most likely), 2 not excluded; spot 2: multilayer, thick (several to tens of layers, assumed)
properties.source: E2g–A1g separation 62.0 (spot 1) vs 64.7 (spot 2); Si attenuation ~10x; Berkdemir et al. 2013 (recalled, verify)

properties.name: phase
properties.source: E2g ~355 and A1g ~418–420 with the 2LA/LA(M) set; no 1T-specific modes observed in 120–600 cm-1

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: E2g is unchanged between spots, so there is no clear in-plane strain signal. The A1g downshift on spot 1 could also be doping or heating (see caveats).

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: A1g softening on spot 1 is compatible with electron doping, but it is not diagnostic without a PL or gating measurement

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: No defect-activated band (e.g., D-like or strongly activated LA(M)) is evident in 120–600 cm-1; 2LA and E2g widths (4.0–4.4 cm-1) are close to the ~3.5 cm-1 Si instrument width, so linewidths cannot resolve defect broadening

properties.name: L_D_nm
properties.value: not applicable (WS2 has no graphene-like defect-distance relation used here)

caveats: Heating and resonance: 514.5 nm lies near the WS2 B-exciton, so intensities and possibly peak positions are sensitive to laser power and heating. Thin flakes on SiO2 heat differently from thick regions. Heating downshifts both modes and may contribute to the 2.8 cm-1 A1g downshift on spot 1. The separation Δ is less sensitive to heating than A1g alone, but not immune.

Doping and strain also shift A1g and E2g. CVD WS2 is often electron-doped (chalcogen vacancies), and substrate strain varies across triangles. A1g softening on spot 1 could come from doping rather than thickness, and this data alone cannot separate them.

Line overlap: the E2g band is a shoulder about 4 cm-1 from the 2LA(M) band, and the spectrometer resolution (~3.5 cm-1, from the Si width) is similar to the E2g width. The E2g centre on spot 1 (355.3) therefore has a systematic uncertainty of perhaps ±0.5 cm-1. Without a dedicated second measurement the E2g assignment on spot 1 is probable but not proven.

Alternative reading of spot 1: the dominant 351 band could be an E2g mode softened by ~4 cm-1, not 2LA(M). I consider this less likely because the 355 shoulder is clearly present and the E2g softening would be unusual, but the data do not fully exclude it.
Calibration: the Si line gives an offset of +0.1–0.2 cm-1 relative to 520.7 cm-1. Absolute positions could shift by that amount. The separation Δ is unaffected.

Intensities and Si ratio: no bare SiO2/Si reference, laser power, acquisition time, objective or spot size were supplied, so the Si attenuation cannot be turned into an absolute thickness. Focus, SiO2 thickness (interference) and island edges within the spot also change the Si signal.

Continuum: the excess continuum on spot 1 (~80 counts above 440 cm-1) could be broad luminescence, a baseline or cosmic-ray-removal difference, or stray light. Its origin cannot be assigned from 120–600 cm-1 data.

Literature values are recalled from memory (no internet access in this session, and no reference files in the folder). The cited numbers (Δ ranges, LA(M) and 2LA(M) at 514.5 nm, Si 520.7 cm-1) should be checked against the original papers before use. The ranges quoted are approximate.
Single spectrum per spot with no repeats or error bars beyond the fit uncertainties. Fit errors do not capture reproducibility across the island.

Monolayer identity is not established by Raman alone: a monolayer shows strong, single-peak direct-gap PL near 2.0 eV, and bilayers show a weaker, shifted PL. Raman layer-number discrimination in the 120–600 cm-1 window is limited to the Δ and resonance cues.
questions_for_user: Is the spot 1 PL spectrum available? A monolayer should show a strong, single direct-gap PL peak near 2.0 eV (~620 nm). This is the most direct monolayer test and is outside the 120–600 cm-1 window.
Can you provide ultra-low-frequency Raman (roughly 10–60 cm-1, shear and breathing modes)? Their presence and position give an unambiguous layer count and would settle 1L vs 2L.
What are the laser power, acquisition time, objective and spot size? Heating and resonance depend on power, and the spot size tells us whether spot 1 includes island edges or neighbouring regions.
Do you have a bare SiO2/Si reference spectrum taken under identical conditions? That would turn the ~10x Si attenuation into a quantitative thickness estimate, given the SiO2 thickness.
Was the Si 520.7 cm-1 reference measured or is the spectrometer calibration documented? Absolute positions depend on this, though the A1g–E2g separation does not.
Do you have an AFM height profile across the island? A 1L WS2 step is typically ~0.7–1 nm on SiO2 (roughly), and it would independently confirm the layer count.
Is the spectrum from a single point or a map? Repeats or a map across the triangle would show whether spot 1 is uniform and would reduce the uncertainty on the E2g shoulder.
Is the 120–600 cm-1 window intended? A wider window (to ~3500 cm-1 for PL and second-order features) would test the continuum difference between the spots.
citations: Berkdemir, A. et al. Identification of individual and few layers of WS2 using Raman spectroscopy. Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013) — layer-dependent E2g/A1g positions and Δ for WS2; 514.5 nm spectra (values recalled from memory, not re-checked here)
Lee, C. et al. Anomalous lattice vibrations of single- and few-layer MoS2. ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010) — A1g stiffening with layer number (MoS2 analogue; recalled from memory)
Temple, P. A. & Hathaway, C. E. Multiphonon Raman spectrum of silicon. Phys. Rev. B 7, 3685 (1973) — Si first-order Raman line at 520.7 cm-1 used as the calibration reference (recalled from memory)
limits: Only the two CSV files in the folder were used. No reference spectra, metadata beyond the stated conditions, or literature access were available in this session, so literature numbers are from memory and marked as such.

The peak fits are Lorentzian least-squares fits over fixed windows; pseudo-Voigt and window-choice checks gave the same centres to ±0.02 cm-1, but the fit residuals are large (reduced chi² ~ 170–190) relative to the noise, so absolute line-shape details are approximate.
Laser power, spot size, acquisition time, polarisation and any Si reference were not given, so absolute intensities, heating and thickness-from-Si-attenuation are not quantified.
The monolayer question cannot be answered definitively from this spectrum: Δ = 62.0 cm-1 is consistent with monolayer but also with bilayer, and PL, ULF Raman or AFM are needed to decide.
